items.title: Iliza Shlesinger: A Different Animal

items.title: Hasan Minhaj: Off with His Head

items.overview: Telling truths and spilling secrets, comedy legend Katt Williams lets loose in this no-holds-barred stand-up special.

With her signature delivery and celebrated gift for storytelling, Tig’s new hour hits all the right notes.

items.overview: Ricky Gervais dishes out controversial takes on political correctness and oversensitivity in a taboo-busting comedy special about the end of humanity.

items.listTitle: Kevin Hart & Chris Rock: Headliners Only

items.overview: From back in the day to the top of their game, Kevin Hart and Chris Rock offer an unparalleled, behind-the-scenes look at their friendship and careers.

items.title: Maria Bamford: Local Act
items.overview: Watch as beloved comedian Maria Bamford reveals the true joy and sense of community involved with being an L.A. standup in her new stripped-down special, Local Comic. Best known as the star of the Netflix series, Lady Dynamite and the cult web series, The Maria Bamford Show. With the release of her new memoir "Sure, I’ll Join Your Cult", she recently added NY Times best-selling author to her accolades. Local Comic is her sixth standup special, adding a brilliant new hour of intimately personal comedy to her existing body of critically praised works.

items.title: Stavros Halkias: Fat Rascal
items.overview: A snapshot of a man whose many vices are actively getting the best of him and a collection of observations, interesting experiences, and sexual embarrassments from two years of non-stop touring

items.listTitle: Mike Birbiglia: The Old Man and the Pool
items.title: Mike Birbiglia: The Old Man and the Pool
items.overview: Comedian Mike Birbiglia dives headlong into mortality, medical tests, nature's pillows and an overchlorinated YMCA pool in this candid one-man show.

items.overview: From his problem with protection crystals to his beef with social media trolls, comedian Matt Rife holds nothing back in this rollicking stand-up special.

items.overview: In his first stand-up special, Trevor Wallace introduces you to the real-life characters he's come face-to-face with, as he navigates male birth control, smoking oregano, his unique birds-and-the-bees talk, experiencing his first Buc-ee's, the red flags of dating, and the worst thing you could ever order on a date.

items.title: Dina Hashem: Dark Little Whispers
items.overview: In a breakout hour of comedy, Dina Hashem discusses everything from death threats and existential dilemmas, to relationship problems, quiet people, and her upbringing as a first generation Arab-American.

Her debut special explores her identity as a Black female Muslim, having 12 siblings, and growing up in Harlem.

items.title: Heather McMahan: Son I Never Had
items.overview: Hitting her emergency weight. TikTok therapy. Joking through her dad's eulogy. Comedian Heather McMahan shares all in this relatable stand-up special.

items.title: Chappelle's Home Team - Luenell: Town Business

Watch now so you can remember it later as the ultimate cult classic!

items.listTitle: Sam Jay: Salute Me or Shoot Me
items.title: Sam Jay: Salute Me or Shoot Me

items.listTitle: Josh Pugh: Live From Birmingham Town Hall

A show about the last two years of his life, trying for a baby and losing Captain Tom's Birthday Cards

With audience in tow, he rants about the downfall of American society and how letting go may be our last hope in this chaotic yet surprisingly optimistic view of our inevitable demise and the cackling laughter we can enjoy while watching it die.

items.title: Kevin Hart: Reality Check
items.overview: Things are about to get real in this unforgettable night of comedy. Comedian Kevin Hart is as funny as ever as he processes his growing family, fame, mentions on Black Twitter, and more. Hart returns for his first stand-up special in three years with a bang, performing from Resort World in Las Vegas while cracking up a live sold-out crowd through candid conversation. Pure honesty inspires genuine humor in this tell-all comedy special.

items.title: Tom Segura: Sledgehammer
items.overview: From his dad's unusual deathbed confession to watching his mom get high, Tom Segura tells blisteringly candid stories about marriage, mortality and more.

items.listTitle: Rob Schneider: Woke Up in America
items.title: Rob Schneider: Woke Up in America

items.title: Wanda Sykes: I'm an Entertainer
items.overview: The comedy icon sounds off on parenting with her French wife, the perils of public bathrooms and why she's tired of going high when others go low.

items.title: Hannah Gadsby: Something Special
items.overview: A panicky proposal. A novelty wedding cake. A fateful bunny encounter. Hannah Gadsby shares tales of love and marriage in this feel-good comedy special.

While most of us were busy giving up on baking in the lockdowns, Tommy aimed for the heavens, taking flying lessons and nailing his first solo flight (well, sort of). Lizzy's show is an hour of big laughs and good times from a comedian whose profile has exploded in a few short years.

items.title: Mae Martin: SAP
items.overview: From a mythical moose encounter to the gender spectrum in "Beauty and the Beast," Mae Martin reflects on a world off its axis in this comedy special.

items.title: Kyle Kinane: Shocks & Struts
items.overview: With his gruff voice, gentle heart, and ill-fated confidence around hotel buffets, Kyle delivers an hour of keen commentary and messy adventure.

items.title: Bert Kreischer: Razzle Dazzle
items.overview: Shameless — and shirtless — as ever, Bert spills on bodily emissions, being bullied by his kids and the explosive end to his family's escape room outing.

items.title: Kelsey Cook: The Hustler
items.overview: Kelsey got divorced one week before the pandemic. Perfect timing. So while her friends used the time to get sober or get fit, Kelsey spent the pandemic getting used to divorced life. Hear about it in her hilarious new hour, The Hustler.

items.title: Chris Rock: Selective Outrage
items.overview: Chris Rock delivers an electric stand-up set on non-racist yoga pants, spoiling his kids, the Kardashians and his thoughts on the Will Smith fiasco.

items.title: Marlon Wayans: God Loves Me
items.overview: Filmed at the Center Stage Theater in Atlanta, Wayans delivers a hilarious hour-long performance, unleashing his spot-on impressions and fearless physical comedy to address one of the most infamous recent events in pop culture – “the slap” that took place at the 94th Academy Awards® ceremony.

items.title: Lavell Crawford: THEE Lavell Crawford
items.overview: Lavell Crawford dives into the issues of getting older without the shame and with all the sarcasm. From experiencing his first bidet to paying HOA fees, Crawford brings playfulness to life's delicate situations that arise as we become more domesticated and seasoned.

items.title: Sommore: Queen Chandelier
items.overview: This Queen of Comedy shines as she takes the stage to sound off on her suspicion of free stuff, social media prayer requests, fake lashes and ugly shoes.

items.title: Kathleen Madigan: Hunting Bigfoot
items.overview: Award winning comedian Kathleen Madigan delivers another great hour of stand up focusing on her family, the Road, the Midwest, boxed wine and her plan of action if she were to hit a Bigfoot.

items.listTitle: Josh Johnson: Up Here Killing Myself
items.title: Josh Johnson: Up Here Killing Myself
items.overview: In this comedic exploration of black mental health and self discovery, comedian Josh Johnson  shares with his therapist, and the audience, his thoughts on growing up without money, grieving, and firing his first gun. There is no subject too big, small, or intimate for Josh to parse through in his first Peacock comedy special.

items.title: Jim Jefferies: High n' Dry
items.overview: No topic is off limits for Jim Jefferies as he muses on stoned koalas, his dad’s vasectomy confusion and choosing between his hair and his sex drive.

items.listTitle: Marc Maron: From Bleak to Dark
items.title: Marc Maron: From Bleak to Dark
items.overview: Over the course of a hilarious and deeply personal hour, Maron explores such universal topics as getting older, antisemitism and faith, and the superiority of having cats over children – especially during the pandemic.

items.title: Marcella Arguello: Bitch, Grow Up!
items.overview: Arguello couples her larger-than-life stage presence with her brutally honest take on post-pandemic hook ups and why broke men are better in bed, an exploration of how “Beauty and the Beast” triggered an epiphany, and a self-reflection on her middle school D.A.R.E. essay.

items.listTitle: Dr Jason Leong: Ride with Caution
items.title: Dr Jason Leong: Ride with Caution
items.overview: In his latest stand-up special, former doctor Jason Leong shares his diagnoses on aging, the absurdity of middle-aged cycling enthusiasts and more.

items.title: Nigel Ng: The HAIYAA Special
items.overview: Uncle Roger and his nephew Nigel Ng present The HAIYAA Special, filmed on their sold out world tour. In this two-part special, Uncle Roger roasts the crowd, while Nigel delivers side-splitting commentary on life and culture. Allergic to MSG and inappropriate jokes? You've been warned.

items.title: Nate Bargatze: Hello World
items.overview: Grammy nominated comedian Nate Bargatze delivers his family friendly take on a variety of topics including disadvantages of being the first born, the challenges of playing golf with your wife, and what happens when a bald eagle touches your head

items.title: Cheeseburger
items.overview: No topic is safe in this unfiltered stand-up set from Andrew Santino as he skewers everything from global warming to sex injuries to politics.

items.title: Tim Minchin: Back
items.overview: After selling out his world tour in record breaking time and receiving rave reviews, internationally renowned, award-winning musician, comedian, actor, writer and composer, Tim Minchin is back... Filmed in front of a live audience at London's Shepherd's Bush Empire, Back is a musical comedy spectacle of 'Old Songs, New Songs, F*** You Songs', showcasing material from all corners of Minchin's eclectic repertoire. A hilarious display of his extraordinary wit, musical virtuoso, self-mockery and philosophical observations, Back is a truly unique and unmissable show.

items.title: Best of Stand-Up 2022
items.overview: From Bill Burr to Ali Wong, Gabriel Iglesias to Trevor Noah, Taylor Tomlinson to Jo Koy, check out the best jokes from Netflix's 2022 stand-up specials.

items.title: Chelsea Handler: Revolution
items.overview: Chelsea Handler lets loose on her life choices, rowdy rescue dogs, dating frustrations, and why society owes women an apology.

items.title: Vir Das: Landing
items.overview: Vir Das dives deep into his childhood in India, the perils of outrage and finding his feet in the world for his fourth Netflix stand-up special.

items.title: Tom Papa: What a Day!
items.overview: Tom doles out truths about post-marriage intimacy, his problematic pet pug and why men are to blame for most of life's inconveniences.

items.title: Daniel Sloss: Socio
items.overview: The new comedy special from the creator of Netflix hit shows 'Dark' & 'Jigsaw' and HBO special 'X'. Toured around the world in 2017 – 2018, filmed in Texas in 2019, and released in 2022.

items.title: Sebastian Maniscalco: Is it Me?
items.overview: In a lively stand-up set, Sebastian acts out life's little agonies, from school drop-offs to off-leash dogs to date nights with his wife.

items.title: Romesh Ranganathan: The Cynic
items.overview: Going back to his hometown of Crawley, England, Romesh Ranganathan will talk about vegan-ism, his kids - and offers a peek into the making of his comedy special.

items.listTitle: Trevor Noah: I Wish You Would
items.title: Trevor Noah: I Wish You Would
items.overview: Emmy-winning comedian Trevor Noah talks learning German, speaking ill of the dead, judging people in horror movies and ordering Indian food in Scotland.

items.title: Deon Cole: Charleen's Boy
items.overview: In an electric stand-up special, Deon Cole ponders romance, racist hotel showers, post-coital bedtime prayers and why he loves women of a certain age.

items.title: Neal Brennan: Blocks
items.overview: From the weird relationship humans have with dogs to how dating a model is like owning a dune buggy, Neal Brennan muses on his life in this stand-up special.

items.title: Panayotis Pascot: Almost
items.overview: Those who still see him as an innocent teen TV correspondent are in for a surprise: French comic Panayotis Pascot is all grown up and ready to get real.

items.listTitle: Chris Redd: Why Am I Like This?
items.title: Chris Redd: Why Am I Like This?
items.overview: In his first HBO Max stand-up special, Chris Redd digs into his days of living life like a music video and realizing that even if he'll never be tall enough to dunk, he can still grow as a person.

items.title: Fortune Feimster: Good Fortune
items.overview: Getting engaged. Getting iced. Getting a mind-blowing butt massage. Fortune Feimster shares uproarious stories from her life in this stand-up special.

items.title: Gabriel Iglesias: Stadium Fluffy
items.overview: Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias makes history as the first comedian to perform at Dodger Stadium in his new special Stadium Fluffy: Live From Los Angeles. Filmed at Netflix Is a Joke: The Festival, Gabriel hilariously shares details about being a Los Angeles native, a recent attempt at extortion towards him, and where he holds the record for receiving the highest fine on stage.

items.title: Iliza Shlesinger: Hot Forever
items.overview: Iliza Shlesinger talks about different topics. She starts from every girl's ugly bra to how all adult men need to own a box spring.

items.title: Hasan Minhaj: The King's Jester
items.overview: Filmed at the historic Brooklyn Academy of Music, Hasan Minhaj returns to Netflix with his second stand-up comedy special Hasan Minhaj: The King's Jester. In this hilarious performance, Hasan shares his thoughts on fertility, fatherhood, and freedom of speech.

items.title: Nick Kroll: Little Big Boy
items.overview: Nick Kroll shares his comedian origin story, his first heartbreak, his strange hypnosis experience and the trash-talking celebrity voice in his head.

items.title: Patton Oswalt: We All Scream
items.overview: Patton riffs on the hazards of aging, his failed shutdown plans, and the day his wife turned into a Valkyrie in this stand-up special he also directed.

items.title: Liss Pereira: Adulting
items.overview: Comedian Liss Pereira gets real about relationships, adulthood and being somewhere in between — not perfect, but not so bad — in a world of extremes.

items.listTitle: Jo Koy: Live from the Los Angeles Forum
items.title: Jo Koy: Live from the Los Angeles Forum
items.overview: Jo Koy owns the stage in a rousing stand-up set about public sneezing, perseverance, the indignities of sleep apnea and getting lost in the Philippines.

items.title: Sheng Wang: Sweet and Juicy
items.overview: Sheng Wang delivers a laid-back set on juicing, mammograms, how snoring is an evolutionary mistake and the existential angst of buying pants from Costco.

items.title: Sam Morril: Same Time Tomorrow
items.overview: Sam Morril delivers his trademark dry and dark punchlines in a stand-up set ranging from problematic fairy tales to biting social commentary.

items.title: Tim Dillon: A Real Hero
items.overview: Tim Dillon rants about fast food, living in Texas, Disney adults and the reason no one should be called a hero.

items.title: Whitney Cummings: Jokes
items.overview: Whitney gets personal about sex injuries and dating younger men, spills on her online photo leak and waxes nostalgic about life before social media.

items.listTitle: David A. Arnold: It Ain't for the Weak
items.title: David A. Arnold: It Ain't for the Weak
items.overview: Performing in his Cleveland hometown, David A. Arnold jokes about marital spats and entitled kids as he shares a behind-the-scenes look at his family.

items.title: Nikki Glaser: Good Clean Filth
items.overview: Comedian and actress Nikki Glaser takes on a range of topics in her brutally-honest yet conversational style. Whether she’s dishing about sex, outlining the do’s and dont’s of dating (and how to trick someone into marriage), or oversharing about her (not-so-private) parts, Glaser delivers an hour of unapologetic and no-holds-barred comedy around topics often considered “taboo,” and showcases her ability to pivot from humiliating moments to being an empowering voice for women: the kind she yearned for as a confused adolescent.

items.listTitle: Bill Burr: Live at Red Rocks
items.title: Bill Burr: Live at Red Rocks
items.overview: Comedian Bill Burr sounds off on cancel culture, feminism, getting bad reviews from his wife and a life-changing epiphany during a fiery stand-up set.

items.listTitle: Dave Chappelle: What's in a Name?
items.title: Dave Chappelle: What's in a Name?
items.overview: Dave Chappelle delivers a speech at his prestigious alma mater that reflects on his comedy roots, his rise to fame and why artists should never behave.

items.title: Cristela Alonzo: Middle Classy
items.overview: In the follow up to her 2016 comedy special, Lower Classy, Cristela Alonzo is back for her second Netflix comedy special, Middle Classy. With more money and a smile big enough to show off her hard earned new teeth, Cristela is living the American Dream. She hilariously shares the joys of aging in her forties, her first ever experience with a gyno, and the importance of family.

items.title: Paul Virzi: Nocturnal Admissions
items.overview: Comedian Paul Virzi takes the stage to spill on awkward drugstore runs, his obsession with crime shows and why his wife sabotaged his fitness goals.

items.title: Joel Kim Booster: Psychosexual
items.overview: Comedian Joel Kim Booster riffs on leaked selfies, dining at P.F. Chang's, keeping secrets and why cats are better than dogs as he hits the stage in LA.

items.listTitle: Jane Fonda & Lily Tomlin: Ladies Night Live
items.title: Jane Fonda & Lily Tomlin: Ladies Night Live
items.overview: Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin host an iconic celebration of women in comedy with stand-up sets from Cristela Alonzo, Margaret Cho, Michelle Buteau and more.

items.listTitle: Pete Davidson Presents: The Best Friends
items.title: Pete Davidson Presents: The Best Friends
items.overview: Pete Davidson jokes about rumors, free plane rides and his very weird year as he invites his friends onstage for a night of stand-up comedy and music.

items.title: Amy Schumer Presents: Parental Advisory
items.overview: Amy Schumer welcomes her favorite comedians to the stage in this special about family life, from the pressures of parenting to the joys of remarriage.

items.title: Stand Out: An LGBTQ+ Celebration
items.overview: A group of LGBTQ+ comedians get together to celebrate a brand of queer comedy. Legends, headliners, and emerging talent all perform at The Greek Theatre for an unforgettable queer stand-up event.

items.listTitle: Bill Burr Presents: Friends Who Kill
items.title: Bill Burr Presents: Friends Who Kill
items.overview: In a night of killer comedy, Bill Burr hosts a showcase of his most raucous stand-up comic pals as they riff on everything from COVID to Michael Jackson.

items.title: Norm Macdonald: Nothing Special
items.overview: In his final comedy special, Norm Macdonald ponders casinos, cannibalism, living wills and why you have to be ready for whatever life throws your way.

items.title: Bo Burnham: The Inside Outtakes
items.overview: Exactly one year after the release of the one man show, "Bo Burnham: Inside" (made in one room, by one person, throughout the pandemic,) comes a series of unseen outtakes, deleted scenes, alternative versions of songs, and new songs unused from the special.

items.title: Ricky Gervais: SuperNature
items.overview: With his signature pitch-black sense of humor, Ricky Gervais takes the stage at the London Palladium in this provocative stand-up comedy special.

items.title: Katt Williams: World War III
items.overview: Katt Williams riffs on truth, lies, chicken wing shortages and the war on drugs in this electrifying stand-up special filmed in Las Vegas.

items.title: Christina P: Mom Genes
items.overview: Comedian Christina P examines the joys and drags of parenting, partnering and more through a no-nonsense Gen-X lens in this special.

items.title: Chris Distefano: Speshy Weshy
items.overview: Fueled by six martinis and a sold-out crowd, comedian Chris Distefano talks getting yelled at on social media, and why he is waiting for his dad to die.

items.title: David Spade: Nothing Personal
items.overview: David Spade riffs on the humiliations of doctor visits, lemur season in paradise, falling for clickbait and the one selfie he can never get right.

items.title: Marlon Wayans Presents: The Headliners
items.overview: Taped live at the Belasco Theatre in Los Angeles, this hour-long special features the comedic stylings of multi-hyphenate legend Marlon Wayans and five up-and-coming stand-ups. Serving as emcee, Wayans shines the spotlight on actor D.C. Ervin, social media star Tony Baker, niece and stand-up comic Chaunté Wayans, writer Sydney Castillo, and noted “closer” Esau McGraw.

items.title: Bill Maher: #Adulting
items.overview: Filmed at Miami’s Fillmore Theater, Bill Maher’s latest stand-up special sees the acclaimed comedian, host, and satirist take the stage for a hilarious and scathing hour of his signature commentary on the latest hot-button issues.

items.title: Ronny Chieng: Speakeasy
items.overview: Ronny Chieng shares his rage at online critics, gratitude for nerds, bewilderment with irrational skeptics and unique cure for racism in this special.

items.title: Jerrod Carmichael: Rothaniel
items.overview: Features Jerrod Carmichael in a standup comedy show at the legendary Blue Note Jazz Club in New York City.

items.title: Mike Epps: Indiana Mike
items.overview: Filmed at the Walker Theatre in his hometown of Indianapolis, with an audience that includes the Mayor, the Indiana Pacers, and his criminal lawyer since 1992, Mike Epps returns for his third hour-long Netflix comedy special. Epps exclaims what he loves about Indiana, his parents’ legacy and much more.

items.listTitle: Jeff Foxworthy: The Good Old Days
items.title: Jeff Foxworthy: The Good Old Days
items.overview: In his first solo stand-up special in 24 years, Jeff Foxworthy is remembering the good old days. Before cell phones diagnosed our illnesses, were used as cameras, kept us informed 24 hours a day, and before we had to have different passwords for everything. Jeff discusses parenting (your children and your parents), texting, the joy of getting a butt dial, conversations with his wife and recalls a much simpler time (or was it?).

items.listTitle: Catherine Cohen: The Twist...? She's Gorgeous
items.title: Catherine Cohen: The Twist...? She's Gorgeous
items.overview: Put on your pink rhinestone rompers for a sparkling evening of comedy cabaret with Catherine Cohen filmed at the iconic Joe’s Pub in New York City.

items.title: Taylor Tomlinson: Look at You
items.overview: Breakups. Therapy. Bangs. Taylor's gone through some stuff since her quarter-life crisis, and she spins her mental health journey into insightful comedy.

items.listTitle: Mo Gilligan: There's Mo to Life
items.title: Mo Gilligan: There's Mo to Life
items.overview: Mo Gilligan breaks down his days as a broke teenager, working in retail, relationship dynamics, annoying talk show producers and more in this special.

items.title: Ali Wong: Don Wong
items.overview: In her third Netflix stand-up special, Ali Wong reveals her wildest fantasies, the challenges of monogamy and how she really feels about single people.

items.title: Only Jokes Allowed
items.overview: Six of South Africa's top comedians take center stage and showcase their talent in this collection of short stand-up sets.

items.listTitle: Ms. Pat: Y'all Wanna Hear Something Crazy?
items.title: Ms. Pat: Y'all Wanna Hear Something Crazy?
items.overview: Ms. Pat finds laughter in the absurdities of parenting, pet lovers and very unfortunate lip trends as she unpacks a painful past with humor and honesty.

items.listTitle: Kapil Sharma: I'm Not Done Yet
items.title: Kapil Sharma: I'm Not Done Yet
items.overview: From the liquid courage behind his tweets to the sobering realities of making it in Mumbai, Kapil's pouring his heart out — with a heavy glug of humor.

items.title: Aziz Ansari: Nightclub Comedian
items.overview: After another year of lockdowns, Aziz takes the stage to skewer pandemic life, quarantines, vaccine cards, celebrity side-gigs, smartphones and more.

items.title: Moses Storm: Trash White
items.overview: Comedian Moses Storm recounts memories of growing up poor, dumpster diving for food, breaking into country clubs, squaring off with carjackers while naked, and more in this hilarious and heartfelt debut standup special.

items.title: Jim Gaffigan: Comedy Monster
items.overview: Comedy icon Jim Gaffigan offers some thoughts on the hot mess that was 2021, as well as his takes on marching bands, billionaires in space, and more.

items.title: Louis C.K.: Sorry
items.overview: Louis C.K.'s stand-up comedy special that discusses sex, society, the Boy Scouts, pandemics, and other topics.

items.title: Matt Rife: Only Fans
items.overview: Comedian Matt Rife discusses his world of deceptive good looks, women and even a charismatic perspective of the world's more pressing topics.

items.title: Russell Howard: Lubricant
items.overview: This two-part special features comic Russell Howard's delayed-yet-delighted return to the stage and a look at his life during an unexpected lockdown.

items.title: Nicole Byer: BBW (Big Beautiful Weirdo)
items.overview: Nicole takes the stage at the Gramercy Theatre for a HOT new set, discussing everything from how she basically is a vegan (she's just doing her part), what she's looking for in a man, and just how crazy this past year-and-a-half has been.

items.title: Mo Amer: Mohammed in Texas
items.overview: In his hometown of Houston, Mo Amer takes on pandemic panic, disappointing Bradley Cooper, hummus appropriation and the subtle art of cursing in Arabic.

items.listTitle: Even More Funny Women of a Certain Age
items.title: Even More Funny Women of a Certain Age
items.overview: Golden Globe winner Teri Hatcher joins the stage with some of the funniest women in comedy for one night of over-the-top, uninhibited stand-up.

items.title: Michael Che: Shame the Devil
items.overview: Michael Che returns to the stage in Oakland and tackles American patriotism, Black leadership, jealous exes, loose bears, mental health and more.

items.title: Aida Rodriguez: Fighting Words
items.overview: For her first hourlong stand-up special, comedian/actress/producer Aida Rodriguez takes the stage in the Bronx to tackle the issues of the day – not just because they’re ripped from the headlines, but because they’re in the pages of her personal life story. With her grounded and unapologetic point of view, Rodriguez gets candid about being worn out from political comedy, embracing both sides of her heritage, getting back into the dating game, and so much more.

items.title: Roy Wood Jr.: Imperfect Messenger
items.overview: Roy Wood Jr. discusses the difference between "ancestors" and "forefathers," why Leonardo DiCaprio is the greatest white ally ever and how celebrities use fame to get people out of prison.

items.title: Theo Von: Regular People
items.overview: Theo Von shares stories of his most memorable childhood friends, offers tips on how to effectively avoid work, and recounts the time he tried to play matchmaker in his hometown.

items.title: Dave Chappelle: The Closer
items.overview: As he closes out his slate of comedy specials, Dave takes the stage to try and set the record straight — and get a few things off his chest.

items.title: Ahir Shah: Dots
items.overview: British comedian Ahir Shah mixes philosophical inquiry, personal examination, and sweet gags in his first ever stand-up special, exploring identity, faith, family, and the desire for certainty in uncertain times.

items.listTitle: Marlon Wayans: You Know What It Is
items.title: Marlon Wayans: You Know What It Is
items.overview: Marlon explores his greatest fears onstage whilst he explains his prominent consternation and trepidation.

items.listTitle: Phil Wang: Philly Philly Wang Wang
items.title: Phil Wang: Philly Philly Wang Wang
items.overview: Phil Wang explores race, romance, politics and his mixed British-Malaysian heritage in this special filmed at the London Palladium.

items.title: Rose Matafeo: Horndog
items.overview: Rose Matafeo has kissed nearly 10 men in her life, AKA she’s a total horndog. But what is horniness? Is it that intangible essence of excitement and adventure that has inspired humankind since the dawn of time? An understanding of the overwhelming power of love as the key to true personal flourishing? Or is it simply wanting to bone everyone, all the time? Recorded at The Ambassadors Theatre, London.

items.title: Josh Johnson: # (Hashtag)
items.overview: Comedian Josh Johnson landed his first comedy special, and fans at home will get to see it. The special features Johnson’s humor on variety of topics — from things women expect in their relationships to the effects of the pandemic on our social lives. He also will consider whether his friend’s bird is racist.

items.title: Chris Gethard: Half My Life
items.overview: This comedy special sees Chris Gethard deliver his blend of hard-hitting stand up and storytelling at small venues across the country at the end of 2019, with documentary footage that shows the reality of what life on the road is really like for a touring comedian.

items.title: Bo Burnham: Inside
items.overview: Stuck in COVID-19 lockdown, US comedian and musician Bo Burnham attempts to stay sane and happy by writing, shooting and performing a one-man comedy special.

items.title: Lavell Crawford: The Comedy Vaccine
items.overview: Lavell Crawford performs his fifth stand-up comedy special in Tempe, Arizona focusing on COVID-19. Lavell shares his views on mask culture, fatherhood and why 2020 was the best year to fart in public.

items.title: Carmen Christopher: Street Special
items.overview: In his debut comedy special, Carmen Christopher does stand-up in the toughest room of all: The streets of New York City.

items.title: Eddie Izzard: Wunderbar
items.overview: Filmed during Eddie’s 2019 tour, Wunderbar exemplifies Eddie’s unique, surreal view of life, love, history and her ‘theory of the universe’.

items.title: Loyiso Gola: Unlearning
items.overview: South African comedian Loyiso Gola serves up filter-free humor as he riffs about race, identity, politics, and a school prank gone embarrassingly wrong!

items.title: Danny Jolles: Six Parts
items.overview: A comedy special by Danny Jolles

items.listTitle: Nate Bargatze: The Greatest Average American
items.title: Nate Bargatze: The Greatest Average American
items.overview: Nate Bargatze touches on Zoom comedy shows, losing his phone, hotel breakfast fails, animal caddies, new math and much more in this special.

items.title: Brian Regan: On the Rocks
items.overview: Brian Regan tackles the big issues weighing on him, including aging, time, obsessive behavior, backpacks on airplanes, ungrateful horses and raisins.

items.title: Patrice O'Neal: Killing Is Easy
items.overview: A documentary about the life and career of controversial stand-up comedian, Patrice O'Neal, who released only one special before his death in 2011.

items.listTitle: Mary Lynn Rajskub: Live from the Pandemic
items.title: Mary Lynn Rajskub: Live from the Pandemic
items.overview: Mary Lynn takes the stage- her garage, to try to make sense of her career, home life, and love life during a global pandemic.

items.title: Best of Stand-Up 2020
items.overview: From Jerry Seinfeld to Leslie Jones, Kevin Hart to Hannah Gadsby, laugh along with the funniest bits from Netflix's 2020 stand-up comedy specials.

items.listTitle: London Hughes: To Catch A D*ck
items.title: London Hughes: To Catch A D*ck
items.overview: London Hughes, the sauciest comedian to come out of the UK, takes us on a brilliant and bold tour of her d*ck catching history.

items.listTitle: Rhys Nicholson: Live at the Athenaeum
items.title: Rhys Nicholson: Live at the Athenaeum
items.overview: Rhys Nicholson flexes his biting humor as he discusses horse tranquilizers, angry letters from viewers, and more in this stand-up special.

items.listTitle: James Acaster: Cold Lasagne Hate Myself 1999
items.title: James Acaster: Cold Lasagne Hate Myself 1999
items.overview: On December 17th 2019, I, James Acaster, filmed my 2019 tour show Cold Lasagne Hate Myself 1999 at EartH in Hackney. It was a show about the best year of my life (1999) and the worst year of my life (2017), I wore a very nifty jacket for it and I looked extremely cool.

items.title: Ari Eldjárn: Pardon My Icelandic
items.overview: Comedian Ari Eldjárn pokes fun at Nordic rivalries, Hollywood’s take on Thor, the whims of toddlers and more.

items.title: Nate: A One Man Show
items.overview: Tough talk takes a soft turn as Nate, played by comedian Natalie Palamides, explores humor, heartbreak, sexuality and consent — with a live audience.

items.title: Dave Chappelle: Unforgiven
items.overview: Dave Chapelle tells a few stories from his childhood, including his early career as a comic and being hustled on the street, whilst discussing an overarching narrative of HBO airing Chapelle Show without Dave being paid for it.

items.title: Kevin Hart: Zero F**ks Given
items.overview: Kevin Hart serves up laughs and brick oven pizza from the comfort of his home, and dishes on male group chats, sex after 40 and life with COVID-19.

items.listTitle: Colin Quinn & Friends: A Parking Lot Comedy Show
items.title: Colin Quinn & Friends: A Parking Lot Comedy Show
items.overview: Colin Quinn and his friends haven't performed comedy in months thanks to the pandemic. So they got together and performed in a parking lot. What could go wrong?

items.title: Sarah Cooper: Everything's Fine
items.overview: Comedian and Trump lip-synching sensation Sarah Cooper tackles politics, race and other light topics in a sketch special packed with celebrity guests.

items.listTitle: Lewis Black: Thanks For Risking Your Life
items.title: Lewis Black: Thanks For Risking Your Life
items.overview: Lewis Black, heir to the George Carlin throne of the comedy rant, performed this set just days after the rest of America shut down (the show was allowed to go on because it was in a sovereign Native American venue), so his commentary covers our current Corona-induced anxiety and his own hilarious frustration over The-Orange-One-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named.

items.title: Michelle Buteau: Welcome to Buteaupia
items.overview: Scene-stealing queen Michelle Buteau dazzles with real talk on relationships, parenthood, cultural differences and the government workers who adore her.

items.title: Dr Jason Leong: Hashtag Blessed
items.overview: In this stand-up special, former doctor Jason Leong gives his diagnoses on the nonsense of traditional healers, business-class show-offs and more.

items.title: Michael McIntyre: Showman
items.overview: Charming comic Michael McIntyre talks family, technology, sharks, accents and the time he confused himself for a world leader in this stand-up special.

items.title: Beth Stelling: Girl Daddy
items.overview: Comedian Beth Stelling takes the stage at Minneapolis’ Varsity Theater to talk sex, drugs, and babies in her hilarious new special Beth Stelling: Girl Daddy. Musing on the ways that sexual pleasure is different for men and women, Stelling’s not ashamed to admit that she always thinks her massage therapist is falling for her – and is not afraid to call male comedians out for making lazy #MeToo jokes. Stelling also shares her takes on being a relationship person, having reverse body dysmorphia, alternative wedding traditions, her relationship with her Orlando-based actor father whose personality is “Fox News,” talking sex with her may-as-well-be-virginal mom, and how her sisters just love to make babies.

items.listTitle: HA Festival: The Art of Comedy
items.title: HA Festival: The Art of Comedy
items.overview: The HA Festival: The Art of Comedy Special is a non-stereotypical show with a predominantly Latinx cast and crew made with a real budget and for all audiences.

items.listTitle: Rob Schneider: Asian Momma, Mexican Kids
items.title: Rob Schneider: Asian Momma, Mexican Kids
items.overview: Former "Saturday Night Live" star Rob Schneider returns to the stage and shares his take on life, love and dinosaur dreams in this stand-up special. Ending with a surprise duet performance with his daughter, singer-songwriter Elle King, Rob talks about potty training his young daughters and his own pig potential.

items.title: Sam Jay: 3 in the Morning
items.overview: Comedian and "Saturday Night Live" writer Sam Jay serves up fresh takes on relationships, travel nightmares, the audacity of white people and more.

items.title: Jim Gaffigan: The Pale Tourist
items.overview: In The Pale Tourist, Gaffigan boldly goes where no stand-up comedian has gone before: everywhere. The two hour-long specials were filmed as part of Gaffigan's The Pale Tourist worldwide tour, in which he traveled the world--in each country meeting people, eating the food, and learning a bit about the history. He would then transform those experiences into a stand-up set of all-new material and perform it for locals and expatriates, before heading on to another destination and doing it all over again.

items.title: Jack Whitehall: I'm Only Joking
items.overview: Jack Whitehall hits the stage with hilarious tales about happy couples, life in hotels, human stupidity and his well-traveled father.

items.title: Urzila Carlson: Overqualified Loser
items.overview: Stand-up comedian Urzila Carlson keeps the crowd roaring with her thoughts on recasting "The Biggest Loser," sex tape regrets and boxed wine hangovers.

items.title: Jim Jefferies: Intolerant
items.overview: Between scenes from an excruciating date, Jim Jefferies digs into generational differences, his own bad habits and the shifting boundaries in comedy.

items.title: Hannibal Buress: Miami Nights
items.overview: Mildly successful comedian, Hannibal Buress, performs his second stand-up special in Chicago based on his wild night with the police.

items.listTitle: George Lopez: We'll Do It for Half
items.title: George Lopez: We'll Do It for Half
items.overview: Comedian George Lopez tackles the future and the past of Latinx culture in America, touching on immigration, his tough relatives, aging and much more.

items.title: Eric Andre: Legalize Everything
items.overview: Comedian Eric Andre presents his very first Netflix original stand-up special. Taking the stage in New Orleans, Andre breaks the boundaries of comedy as he critiques the war on drugs, the war on sex, and the war on fart jokes!

items.listTitle: Larry the Cable Guy: Remain Seated
items.title: Larry the Cable Guy: Remain Seated
items.overview: Larry the Cable Guy is back to Git R Done. Remain Seated, his latest solo special, will show you why this Grammy nominated, multi-platinum recording artist, and Billboard award winner is at the top of his game. Coming to you straight from the Rialto Square Theater in Joliet, IL to your seat at home!
From Dave: Normally I wouldn't show you something so unrefined, I hope you understand.

items.listTitle: Yvonne Orji: Momma, I Made It!
items.title: Yvonne Orji: Momma, I Made It!
items.overview: 'Insecure' star Yvonne Orji celebrates her Nigerian-American upbringing in her debut HBO comedy special, which intersperses her stand-up with documentary footage of a trip to Nigeria.

items.listTitle: Kenny Sebastian: The Most Interesting Person in the Room
items.title: Kenny Sebastian: The Most Interesting Person in the Room
items.overview: Fusing his musical and stand-up chops, Kenny Sebastian gets analytical about frumpy footwear, flightless birds and his fear of not being funny enough.

items.title: Hannah Gadsby: Douglas
items.overview: Hannah Gadsby returns for her second special and digs deep into the complexities of popularity, identity, and her most unusual dog park encounter.

items.title: Patton Oswalt: I Love Everything
items.overview: Turning 50. Finding love again. Buying a house. Experiencing existential dread at Denny's. Life comes at Patton Oswalt fast in this stand-up special.

items.title: Tom Gleeson: Joy
items.overview: Australia’s 2019 Gold Logie winner. Chief celebrity interrogator. Host of the highest-rating quiz show on TV. There’s not much Tom Gleeson hasn’t been up to lately. Gleeson is one of the sharpest minds in Australian comedy. His shows are relentlessly hilarious and masterful. Now the world can watch the great man live on stage, in his natural habitat and in the form of his life. Experience the JOY.

items.title: Jerry Seinfeld: 23 Hours to Kill
items.overview: Jerry Seinfeld takes the stage in New York and tackles talking vs. texting, bad buffets vs. so-called "great" restaurants and the magic of Pop Tarts.

items.title: Tom Walker: Very Very
items.overview: A love letter to mime (and to a coat) written by award-winning idiot Tom Walker, who keeps talking during what he insists is a mime show.

items.listTitle: Dan Cummins: Get Outta Here; Devil!
items.title: Dan Cummins: Get Outta Here; Devil!
items.overview: In his third hour special, comic and podcaster Dan Cummins presents some of his most outrageous material to date. Dan mocks those who believe in the lizard illuminati, a flat earth, the notion that you can sell your soul to Satan, and more. Dan even makes fun of himself for once having sex with a banana peel in a grocery store bathroom - nothing's too weird or dark. Dan jokes about his kids, his ongoing hatred of strangers, and even offers to improve the world by killing a lot of people. Enjoy!

items.title: Yours Sincerely, Kanan Gill
items.overview: Revisiting life goals set in a letter written as a teen to his future self, comedian Kanan Gill reports back on if he's lived up to his own expectations.

items.title: Alice Fraser: Savage
items.overview: Alice Fraser's critically acclaimed comedy show, Savage, is about paper towels and how not to murder people who “mean well”. A hilarious and heartbreaking show that walks you through the razor edges of a life stripped bare. How you deal with losing everything, what Buddhists do with rage and how bubble blowers work at funerals. Savage talks about things that are actually sad and also very funny.

items.title: Chris D'Elia: No Pain
items.overview: Chris D'Elia takes the stage in Minneapolis to offer his thoughts on everything from self-censorship to problematic dolphins to lame mutant powers.

items.title: This Is Stand-Up
items.overview: An intimate and revealing insight into the work and lives of Stand-Up Comedians. Some of the biggest names in the game reveal what it's like to pursue this most challenging, yet important art-form.

items.title: Zoë Coombs Marr: Bossy Bottom
items.overview: There is no comedian quite like Zoë. Bossy Bottom is a joyously silly return to very serious stand up from the MICF Most Outstanding Show winner and Edinburgh Best Show nominee.

items.title: Sincerely Louis C.K.
items.overview: Louis C.K. muses on religion, terrorism, small towns, Florida, disabilities, dogs, Auschwitz, marriage, sex, vegans, and his personal sexual controversy, in a live performance from Washington, D.C.

items.title: Tom Segura: Ball Hog
items.overview: Tom Segura scores laughs with uncomfortably candid stories about mothers, fathers, following your dreams — and other things you'd rather not think about.

items.title: Bert Kreischer: Hey Big Boy
items.overview: Still the ultimate comedy party animal, Bert Kreischer tells more stories about parenthood and family life in a stand-up special from Cleveland.

items.listTitle: More Funny Women of a Certain Age
items.title: More Funny Women of a Certain Age
items.overview: Caroline Rhea headlines a cast of the funniest women of standup in a night of uninhibited, outrageous comedy. Starring Caroline Rhea, Carol Leifer, Tammy Pescatelli, Thea Vidale, Carole Montgomery and Julia Scotti.

items.title: Marc Maron: End Times Fun
items.overview: Marc Maron wades through a swamp of vitamin hustlers, evangelicals and grown male nerd children, culminating in a gleefully filthy end-times fantasy.

items.title: Taylor Tomlinson: Quarter-Life Crisis
items.overview: Comedian Taylor Tomlinson is halfway through her 20s — and she's over it. From dating losers to a failed engagement, she takes aim at her life choices.

items.title: David A. Arnold: Fat Ballerina
items.overview: Finally comfortable in his skin, seasoned comic David A. Arnold shares his talent for doing nothing, how he's petty and why divorce saves marriages.

items.listTitle: Pete Davidson: Alive from New York
items.title: Pete Davidson: Alive from New York
items.overview: Comedian and "SNL" star Pete Davidson drops a candid and intimate stand-up special shot live in New York City.

items.title: Whitmer Thomas: The Golden One
items.overview: Thomas reflects on his Alabama childhood and his identity as an “aging emo kid” in LA through stories and songs on topics like dating, drinking, family and his mom’s legacy.

items.title: Sam Morril: I Got This
items.overview: Sam Morril compares wearing a condom to doing volunteer work, wonders if murderers critique each other’s work and recalls befriending a vigilante in Cleveland.

items.title: Tom Papa: You're Doing Great!
items.overview: Comedian Tom Papa takes on body image issues, social media, pets, Staten Island, the "old days" and more in a special from his home state of New Jersey.

items.listTitle: Maria Bamford: Weakness Is the Brand
items.title: Maria Bamford: Weakness Is the Brand
items.overview: Maria Bamford is back and subjectively better than ever! Weakness is her brand, so get ready to feel much better about yourself. This Lady Dynamite explodes onstage (after 2 (two) naps with her husband Scott and 2 old, pillowy dogs). Let her be the poor example from which your greatness can be determined.

items.title: Vir Das: For India
items.overview: From the Vedas to Vasco de Gama to vacuous Bollywood plotlines, comedian Vir Das celebrates the history of India with his one-of-a-kind perspective.

items.title: Fortune Feimster: Sweet & Salty
items.overview: Actor, comedian and writer Fortune Feimster takes the stage and riffs on her southern roots, sexual awakenings, showbiz career and more.

items.title: Leslie Jones: Time Machine
items.overview: From trying to seduce Prince to battling sleep apnea, Leslie Jones traces her evolution as an adult in a joyfully raw and outrageous stand-up special.

items.listTitle: Ronny Chieng: Asian Comedian Destroys America!
items.title: Ronny Chieng: Asian Comedian Destroys America!
items.overview: Comedian Ronny Chieng shares his unapologetic perspective about his journey to America, and what he thinks really makes America great.

items.title: Michelle Wolf: Joke Show
items.overview: Comedian Michelle Wolf takes on outrage culture, massages, childbirth, feminism and much more (like otters) in a stand-up special from New York City.

items.title: Tiffany Haddish: Black Mitzvah
items.overview: On her 40th birthday, Tiffany Haddish drops a bombastic special studded with singing, dancing and raunchy reflections on her long road to womanhood.

items.title: Mike Birbiglia: The New One
items.overview: Comedian Mike Birbiglia hits Broadway with a hilarious yet profound one-man show that recounts his emotional and physical journey to parenthood.

items.listTitle: Lil Rel Howery: Live in Crenshaw
items.title: Lil Rel Howery: Live in Crenshaw
items.overview: Known for his well-crafted storytelling and hilarious impressions of the myriad characters he encounters in life, Lel Rel Howery draws on his personal experiences in his relatable, uproarious stand-up. Howery's HBO stand-up comedy debut was filmed before a live audience at Susan Miller Dorsey High School in Los Angeles.

items.title: Iliza Shlesinger: Unveiled
items.overview: Comedian Iliza Shlesinger dissects her recent wedding with riffs on screeching bachelorette parties, that creepy garter removal tradition and more.

items.title: Seth Meyers: Lobby Baby
items.overview: SNL alumnus and subversive master of late-night Seth Meyers comes out from behind the desk to share some lighthearted stories from his own life.

items.title: Daniel Sloss: X
items.overview: Daniel Sloss discusses a variety of topics, from his love of children, to being a man, in this tastefully dark comedy special.

items.title: Celeste Barber: Challenge Accepted
items.overview: Actor, Comedian, and Social Media Superstar Celeste Barber exposes the stories behind some of her most famous Instagram celebrity parody images, her new relationships with famous people, the pitfalls of being married to someone so much hotter than her, and what it’s like to be an Anti-Influencer.

items.title: Jenny Slate: Stage Fright
items.overview: Jenny Slate's first stand-up special is a mix of stage time, funny stories about adulthood and conversations with family in her childhood home.

items.title: Deon Cole: Cole Hearted
items.overview: Embracing his belief that comedy is the last raw form of expression, Deon Cole explains the right time to thank Jesus and the wrong time to say "welp.".

items.title: Gary Gulman: The Great Depresh
items.overview: In his first HBO comedy special, Gary Gulman offers candid reflections on his struggles with depression through stand-up and short documentary interludes. While speaking to issues of mental health, Gulman also offers his observations on a number of topics, including his admiration for Millennial attitudes toward bullying, the intersection of masculinity and sports, and how his mother's voice is always in his head.

items.title: Nikki Glaser: Bangin'
items.overview: Nikki Glaser bares all in a blistering stand-up special about sex, sobriety and getting over her own insecurities. And she won't spare you the details.

items.title: Mo Gilligan: Momentum
items.overview: Comedian Mo Gilligan blends smooth moves and sharp humor as he riffs on humble beginnings, family dynamics and the complex art of dancing in the club.

items.title: Jeff Dunham: Beside Himself
items.overview: The ventriloquist, Jeff Dunham, taped his second Netflix special in his hometown of Dallas, TX in the American Airlines Center. He returns with his normal cast of characters including Walter, Bubba J, Peanut, José Jalapeño on a Stick, Achmed the Dead Terrorist, and one of his newest additions Larry, a high strung, chain-smoking, on-again, off-again personal adviser to the President.

items.title: Bill Burr: Paper Tiger
items.overview: Comedian Bill Burr talks male feminists, outrage culture, robot sex, and cultural appropriation in this standup comedy special shot in London.

items.title: Dave Chappelle: Sticks & Stones
items.overview: Dave Chappelle takes on gun culture, the opioid crisis and the tidal wave of celebrity scandals in this defiant stand-up special.

items.title: Epilogue: The Punchline
items.overview: Dave's encore from his special Sticks and Stones.

items.title: Simon Amstell: Set Free
items.overview: Honest, introspective comic Simon Amstell digs deep and delivers a uniquely vulnerable stand-up set on love, ego, intimacy and ayahuasca.

items.title: Jim Gaffigan: Quality Time
items.overview: Comedian Jim Gaffigan performs live at the State Theatre in Minneapolis, MN.

items.listTitle: My Favorite Shapes by Julio Torres
items.title: My Favorite Shapes by Julio Torres
items.overview: In this multimedia comedy show, Torres explores his favorite shapes, which include a plexiglass square, a triangle, an oval that wishes he were a circle, a self-conscious cactus and a Ferrero Rocher chocolate that Julio is mad at because she left her little skirt at home. The objects are presented via an industrial conveyer belt and serve as a jumping-off point for fantastical stories, anecdotes and jokes.

items.listTitle: Whitney Cummings: Can I Touch It?
items.title: Whitney Cummings: Can I Touch It?
items.overview: In her fourth stand-up special, Whitney Cummings returns to her hometown of Washington, D.C., and riffs on modern feminism, technology and more.

items.title: Aziz Ansari: Right Now
items.overview: In a comedy special directed by Spike Jonze, Aziz Ansari shares deep personal insights and hilarious takes on wokeness, family and the social climate.

items.title: Katherine Ryan: Glitter Room
items.overview: Fresh from a tour, comedian Katherine Ryan shares shrewd observations about school bullies, revenge bodies and raising a very fancy child.

items.title: Ramy Youssef: Feelings
items.overview: In his first HBO stand-up comedy special, Ramy Youssef shares candid anecdotes about his life as an Egyptian-American comedian, writer, actor and director.

items.title: Mike Epps: Only One Mike
items.overview: In a raw stand-up comedy special, Mike Epps mixes it up as he tackles sexual misconduct, special ed, aging body parts and much more.

items.listTitle: Adam Devine: Best Time of Our Lives
items.title: Adam Devine: Best Time of Our Lives
items.overview: Critically acclaimed comedian, Adam Devine, knows that growing up sucks and is here to tell you why. Filmed in front of a packed house at The Orpheum Theater in his hometown of Omaha, Nebraska, Devine's new Netflix comedy special will give a comedic take on the worst parts of growing up including puberty, parental judgment, and almost dying on your 21st birthday.

items.title: Jo Koy: Comin' in Hot
items.overview: Comedian Jo Koy takes center stage in Hawaii and shares his honest take on island life, ethnicity, fatherhood and more.

items.title: Jeff Dunham: Talking Heads
items.overview: Ventriloquist/comic Jeff Dunham talks about his childhood and his start into the world of ventriloquism.

items.listTitle: Colin Quinn: Red State, Blue State
items.title: Colin Quinn: Red State, Blue State
items.overview: Stand-up comedian Colin Quinn calls out the hypocrisies of the left and the right in this special based on his politically charged Off-Broadway show.

items.title: Wanda Sykes: Not Normal
items.overview: Wanda Sykes tackles politics, reality TV, racism and the secret she'd take to the grave in this rollicking, no-holds-barred stand-up special.

items.title: David Cross: Oh Come On
items.overview: Share the laughter, the tears, the gasps, and the salty language that you've come to know and love. Stare into the abyss one more time until the next time and see what makes David Cross one of the top 400 comics in America today.

items.listTitle: Anthony Jeselnik: Fire in the Maternity Ward
items.title: Anthony Jeselnik: Fire in the Maternity Ward
items.overview: Forging his own comedic boundaries, Anthony Jeselnik revels in getting away with saying things others can't in this stand-up special shot in New York.

items.title: Kevin Hart: Irresponsible
items.overview: Stand-up comedian Kevin Hart talks about his family, travel and a year full of reckless behavior in front of a live sold-out crowd in London.

items.title: Nate Bargatze: The Tennessee Kid
items.overview: Comic Nate Bargatze touches on air travel, cheap weddings, college football, chocolate milk and the perils of ordering coffee in this stand-up special.

items.title: Amy Schumer: Growing
items.overview: Amy Schumer's live stand-up set performed in Chicago where she jokes about marriage, pregnancy and personal growth.

items.title: Emily Heller: Ice Thickeners
items.overview: The comic and writer for HBO’s Barry compares Donald Trump to Air Bud, answers some FAQs about vegetarianism, and recalls telling her personal trainer about her lack of fitness goals.

items.listTitle: Ray Romano: Right Here, Around the Corner
items.title: Ray Romano: Right Here, Around the Corner
items.overview: Ray Romano first cut his stand-up teeth at the Comedy Cellar in New York. Now, in his first comedy special in 23 years, he returns to where it all began.

items.listTitle: Gabriel "Fluffy" Iglesias: One Show Fits All
items.title: Gabriel "Fluffy" Iglesias: One Show Fits All
items.overview: Gabriel "Fluffy" Iglesias discusses his teenage son and encounters with Snoop Dogg, Chris Rock and Vicente Fernández in this stand-up special for 2019.

items.listTitle: Roy Wood Jr.: No One Loves You
items.title: Roy Wood Jr.: No One Loves You
items.overview: Roy Wood Jr. explores some of today's most complicated issues, from the plight of the black superhero to national anthem protests.

items.title: Sebastian Maniscalco: Stay Hungry
items.overview: Sebastian Maniscalco brings an acerbically unique approach to peacocks on planes, life hacks, rich in-laws and life's annoyances in this comedy special.

items.listTitle: Sommore: A Queen With No Spades
items.title: Sommore: A Queen With No Spades
items.overview: Sommore is back for her 4th self-produced comedy special. Filmed at the Beautiful Faena Theater in Miami Beach, she covers topics ranging from her own personal growth and development, to her unique perspective on life, politics and individual choice.

items.title: Ellen DeGeneres: Relatable
items.overview: In her first special since 2003, Ellen revisits her road to stardom and details the heartfelt -- and hilarious -- lessons she's learned along the way.

items.title: Vir Das: Losing It
items.overview: The world's got a lot of problems, but Vir Das has a lot of answers as he discusses travel, religion, his childhood and more in this stand-up special.

items.listTitle: Bumping Mics with Jeff Ross & Dave Attell
items.title: Bumping Mics with Jeff Ross & Dave Attell
items.overview: When Jeff Ross and Dave Attell take the stage, no one is safe. With the help of special guests, they're packing a lot of laughs into one epic weekend.

items.title: Michael Yo: Blasian
items.overview: Family first comedian and bonafide Blasian, Michael Yo, brings his uniquely personal blend of comedy to his debut stand up special. Born and raised in Houston, TX, Michael talks about the issues growing up half Black and Asian in a place where he really stood out. Fast forward to now, navigating marriage and of course his ultimate job as a father to his Black, Asian and White son.

items.title: Trevor Noah: Son of Patricia
items.overview: Trevor Noah gets out from behind the "Daily Show" desk and takes the stage for a stand-up special that touches on racism, immigration, camping and more.

items.listTitle: Dennis Miller: Fake News, Real Jokes
items.title: Dennis Miller: Fake News, Real Jokes
items.overview: Five-time Emmy award winner Dennis Miller takes on the current climate like no other can in Fake News, Real Jokes! From selfies and airline travel to Trump and journalists, he delivers his signature critical assessments in his low key style that has been deemed by The Hollywood Reporter as "the most cerebral, astute and clever standup ever".

items.listTitle: John Leguizamo's Latin History for Morons
items.title: John Leguizamo's Latin History for Morons
items.overview: In this one-man Broadway show, John Leguizamo finds humor and heartbreak as he traces 3,000 years of Latin history in an effort to help his bullied son.

items.title: Paul Virzi: I'll Say This
items.overview: Paul Virzi masterfully balances his edgy New York demeanor with his vulnerability as a husband, father and lover of nerdy things. Paul shares his hatred of political debate on social media, the challenges of manning the gate to heaven, his surprisingly ruthless young daughter and his unintentional sick thoughts.

items.title: Adam Sandler: 100% Fresh
items.overview: Adam Sandler takes his comical musical musings back out on the road, from comedy clubs to concert halls to one very unsuspecting subway station.

items.listTitle: Ron White: If You Quit Listening, I'll Shut Up
items.title: Ron White: If You Quit Listening, I'll Shut Up
items.overview: Ron "Tater Salad" White dishes out his signature brand of cynicism, riffing on sex, celebrity and the sinister habits of wild geese.

items.title: Mo Amer: The Vagabond
items.overview: Arab-American comedian Mo Amer recounts his life as a refugee comic, from traveling with the name Mohammed to his long path to citizenship.

items.title: Joe Rogan: Strange Times
items.overview: Outspoken as ever, comedian Joe Rogan takes on politics, pro wrestling, pot laws, cats, vegans and much more in a stand-up special shot in Boston.

items.title: Leanne Morgan: So Yummy
items.overview: Leanne Morgan exudes southern charm. She is a naturally funny storyteller who gives an honest look at suburban life and the challenges of keeping her husband happy while juggling kids, dogs and cheerleading camp at the same time she’s racing to get her hair highlighted, have a colonoscopy and join weight watchers for the 7th time!  Leanne will take you on a hilarious journey through motherhood and beyond as she finds comedy amidst the chaos.

items.title: D.L. Hughley: Contrarian
items.overview: Comedian D.L. Hughley riffs on politics, "Black Panther," his upbringing and more in a rapid-fire stand-up show at Philadelphia's Merriam Theater.

items.title: Sam Morril: Positive Influence
items.overview: Comedian Sam Morril performs. Topics include why babies seem racist; why porn is more body positive than women's magazines; and an awful customer service experience with an airline.

items.title: Daniel Sloss: Live Shows
items.overview: Comedian Daniel Sloss is ready to find the funny in some very dark topics, from the deeply personal to the truly irreverent.

items.title: Drew Michael
items.overview: Comedian Drew Michael is taking the stage and is holding nothing back in his first HBO stand-up special, in which he navigates his fears, anxieties and insecurities in an unconventional stand-up setting. Michael’s darkly comic, stream-of-consciousness monologue raises questions of identity, narrative, self-awareness and the limits of the medium itself.

items.title: Bert Kreischer: Secret Time
items.overview: Comedian Bert Kreischer is ready to take his shirt off and "party hardy" with his debut Netflix Original stand-up special, Bert Kreischer: Secret Time. Considered one of the best storytellers of his generation, Bert regales the audience at the Trocadero Theatre in Philadelphia with stories about zip-lining with his family, his daughter practicing softball with an imaginary ball, and upstaging ex-NBA player Ralph Sampson at a childhood basketball camp.

items.title: Demetri Martin: The Overthinker
items.overview: With his signature one-liners and drawings, Demetri Martin muses on doughnut holes, dogs, sports bars, the alphabet's most aggressive letters and more.

items.listTitle: Just Another Immigrant: Romesh at the Greek
items.title: Just Another Immigrant: Romesh at the Greek
items.overview: Romesh Ranganathan, a successful comedian in England, moves his entire family to Los Angeles to pursue his lifelong dream of making it as a stand-up comedian in America. He then takes the drastic, and possibly foolish, step of performing his first ever U.S. stand-up show at the six-thousand seat historic Greek Theater.

items.title: Iliza Shlesinger: Elder Millennial
items.overview: Filmed February 23, 2018, aboard the USS Hornet, comedian Iliza Shlesinger brings an ‘elder millennial’ perspective to her audience. Recently engaged, she dives into undeniable truths about life at age 35. Looking back at the insanity of the road traveled and what’s to come, Iliza talks first apartments, a woman's inner she dragon, peacock mating calls, and her newfound urge to squeeze a chubby baby leg.

items.listTitle: Jim Jefferies: This Is Me Now
items.title: Jim Jefferies: This Is Me Now
items.overview: The gleefully irreverent Jefferies skewers “grabby” celebrities, political hypocrisy and his own ill-advised career moves in a brash stand-up special.

items.title: Jim Gaffigan: Noble Ape
items.overview: Jim Gaffigan has made a career out of finding the extraordinary in the ordinary with his hilarious observational style. In his 6th special, he uses humor to deal with the unthinkable & proves that laughter is the best medicine…or is it?

items.title: The Comedy Lineup
items.overview: A diverse group of up-and-coming comedians perform 15-minute sets in this stand-up comedy showcase series.

items.listTitle: W. Kamau Bell: Private School Negro
items.title: W. Kamau Bell: Private School Negro
items.overview: Comedian W. Kamau Bell muses on parenting in the Trump era, "free speech" dustups, woke children's TV and his fear of going off the grid.

items.title: Hannah Gadsby: Nanette
items.overview: The Australian comedian Hannah Gadsby is taking an anti-comedy stance in her newest special.

items.title: Cameron Esposito: Rape Jokes
items.overview: RAPE JOKES is an hourlong standup special centered on sexual assault from a survivor’s perspective. Written and performed by Cameron Esposito, proceeds from the special benefit RAINN, the United States’ largest anti-sexual violence organization.

items.listTitle: Tig Notaro: Happy to Be Here
items.title: Tig Notaro: Happy to Be Here
items.overview: Comedian Tig Notaro unleashes her inner prankster in a playful stand-up special packed with funny anecdotes, parenting confessions and more.

items.title: Ali Wong: Hard Knock Wife
items.overview: Pregnant again, Ali Wong returns to Netflix in her second original stand-up comedy special and gets real on why having kids is not all it's cracked up to be.

items.title: Hari Kondabolu: Warn Your Relatives
items.overview: Hari Kondabolu breaks down identity politics, celebrity encounters, his mango obsession and more in an unpredictable stand-up comedy special.

items.listTitle: John Mulaney: Kid Gorgeous at Radio City
items.title: John Mulaney: Kid Gorgeous at Radio City
items.overview: John Mulaney relays stories from his childhood and "SNL," eviscerates the value of college and laments getting older in this electric comedy special.

items.listTitle: Kevin James: Never Don't Give Up
items.title: Kevin James: Never Don't Give Up
items.overview: Kevin James makes his long-awaited return to stand-up in this family-friendly special, dishing on fatherhood, fans, his disdain for allergies and more.

items.title: Seth Rogen's Hilarity for Charity
items.overview: Seth Rogen and friends combine stand-up, sketches and music for an outrageous comedy special that could only come from the mind of Seth. Guests include Tiffany Haddish, Sarah Silverman, Michelle Wolf, John Mulaney, Michael Che, David Chang, Ike Barinholtz, Chelsea Peretti, Kumail Nanjiani, Jon Lovitz, Jeff Goldblum, Sacha Baron Cohen, Nick Kroll, Post Malone, Chris Hardwick, and Craig Robinson & The Nasty Delicious.

items.title: James Acaster: Repertoire
items.overview: Offbeat comic James Acaster covers the strange, the mundane and everything in between in this collection of four wide-ranging stand-up specials.

items.title: Ricky Gervais: Humanity
items.overview: In his first special in seven years, Ricky Gervais slings his trademark snark at celebrity, mortality and a society that takes everything personally.

items.title: Marlon Wayans: Woke-ish
items.overview: An American stand-up comedy special starring Marlon Wayans who jokes about racism, hip-hop, gay rights, and raising kids.

items.title: Chris Rock: Tamborine
items.overview: Chris Rock takes the stage for his first comedy special in 10 years, filled with searing observations on fatherhood, infidelity and American politics.

items.title: Fred Armisen: Standup for Drummers
items.overview: For an audience of drummers, comedian Fred Armisen shares and demonstrates his thoughts on musical genres, drummer quirks, regional accents and more.

items.title: Todd Glass: Act Happy
items.overview: Try to keep up as comedian Todd Glass delivers rapid-fire stand-up that bounces from his heart attack to his coming out to how to eat a Kit Kat.

items.title: Katt Williams: Great America
items.overview: The king of underground comedy takes the stage in Jacksonville with unflinching riffs on American politics and the raunchy perils of getting old.

items.title: Tom Segura: Disgraceful
items.overview: Tom Segura gives voice to the sordid thoughts you'd never say out loud, with blunt musings on porn, parking lot power struggles, parenthood and more.

items.title: Dave Chappelle: The Bird Revelation
items.overview: Comedy juggernaut Dave Chappelle's fourth Netflix Special, taped on November 20th, 2017 at Los Angeles' Comedy Store.

items.title: Dave Chappelle: Equanimity
items.overview: Comedy legend Dave Chappelle returns to his roots with an all-new stand-up special filmed at the Warner Theatre in Washington, D.C.

items.title: Russell Howard: Recalibrate
items.overview: Self-deprecating comic Russell Howard plows ahead through politics, porn, social media and his own shortcomings. Yet he somehow keeps it positive.

items.title: Judd Apatow: The Return
items.overview: Renowned producer, director and writer Judd Apatow makes his long-awaited return to stand-up comedy with this new special shot in Montreal.

items.title: Michelle Wolf: Nice Lady
items.overview: Comedian Michelle Wolf stars in her first HBO special — an hour of stand-up featuring her observations on feminism, dating, and other social issues.

items.title: Brian Regan: Nunchucks and Flamethrowers
items.overview: Brian Regan takes relatable family humor to new heights as he talks board games, underwear elastic and looking for hot dogs in all the wrong places.

items.title: Jeff Ross Roasts the Border
items.overview: Roastmaster Jeff Ross explores the world surrounding the U.S.-Mexico border, speaking to immigrants, DREAMers, detainees, border patrolers, human traffickers and Trump supporters. Then he puts on a show next to the border wall to roast American immigration policies, random audience volunteers and every ethnicity imaginable.

items.listTitle: Judah Friedlander: America Is the Greatest Country in the United States
items.title: Judah Friedlander: America Is the Greatest Country in the United States
items.overview: Deadpan comic and self-proclaimed world champion Judah Friedlander performs over several nights in New York, explaining why America is No. 1.

items.title: Jack Whitehall: At Large
items.overview: Comedian Jack Whitehall takes the stage to tell stories about drinking, drugs, a Google Maps van and his ongoing rivalry with Robert Pattinson.

items.title: Patton Oswalt: Annihilation
items.overview: Patton Oswalt, despite a personal tragedy, produces his best standup yet. Focusing on the tribulations of the Trump era and life after the loss of a loved one, Oswalt continues his journey to contribute joy to the world.

items.title: Christina P: Mother Inferior
items.overview: Christina Pazsitzky hits Seattle with a biting dose of reality, telling truths about her childhood, getting older and the horrors of giving birth.

items.listTitle: Rodney Carrington: Here Comes the Truth
items.title: Rodney Carrington: Here Comes the Truth
items.overview: Raunchy country comic and musician Rodney Carrington jokes and sings about life in his 40s, poking fun at sex, relationships and gaining weight.

items.title: Jerry Before Seinfeld
items.overview: Jerry Seinfeld returns to the club that gave him his start in the 1970s, mixing iconic jokes with stories from his childhood and early days in comedy.

items.title: Jeff Dunham: Relative Disaster
items.overview: Ventriloquist Jeff Dunham brings his rude, crude and slightly demented posse of puppets to Ireland for a gleeful skewering of family and politics.

items.title: Marc Maron: Too Real
items.overview: Battle-scarred stand-up comedian Marc Maron unleashes a storm of ideas about meditation, mortality, documentary films and our weird modern world.

items.title: Ryan Hamilton: Happy Face
items.overview: Small-town import Ryan Hamilton charms New York with folksy comic observations on big-city life, hot-air ballooning and going to Disney World alone.

items.listTitle: Tiffany Haddish: She Ready! From the Hood to Hollywood!
items.title: Tiffany Haddish: She Ready! From the Hood to Hollywood!
items.overview: In her first stand-up special filmed at the Nate Holden Performing Arts Center, Los Angeles native and rising star Tiffany Haddish tackles subjects ranging from her early days in foster care and being bullied on the playground to getting revenge on ex-boyfriends and introducing Will and Jada Pinkett Smith to Groupon.

items.listTitle: Trevor Noah: There's a Gupta on My stoep
items.title: Trevor Noah: There's a Gupta on My stoep
items.overview: Trevor Noah is back to perform in the biggest comedy show in South African history, in one of Johannesburg's most iconic live performance venues. He returns to where it all started, with all-new material, in his first new South African show since he became  host of the Daily Show.  His biggest stage. His biggest audience. Your biggest laughs.

items.title: Maz Jobrani: Immigrant
items.overview: Iranian American comic Maz Jobrani lights up the Kennedy Center with riffs on immigrant life in the Trump era, modern parenting pitfalls and more.

items.title: Joe Mande's Award-Winning Comedy Special
items.overview: Stand-up comic Joe Mande aims for critical adulation with this special that covers dating shows, "Shark Tank," Jewish summer camp and much more.

items.listTitle: Aditi Mittal: Things They Wouldn't Let Me Say
items.title: Aditi Mittal: Things They Wouldn't Let Me Say
items.overview: Trailblazing comic Aditi Mittal mixes topical stand-up with frank talk about being single, wearing thongs and the awkwardness of Indian movie ratings.

items.title: Erik Griffin: The Ugly Truth
items.overview: With a sharp wit and even sharper tongue, Griffin deconstructs everything from modern romance and profile pictures to calorie counting and Fatburger in this raucous hour of standup.

items.title: The Standups
items.overview: Comedy's freshest voices take the stage in LA for six half-hour specials packed with sly jokes, hilarious anecdotes and awkward confessions.

items.listTitle: Rory Scovel Tries Stand-Up for the First Time
items.title: Rory Scovel Tries Stand-Up for the First Time
items.overview: Comedian Rory Scovel storms the stage in Atlanta, where he shares unfocused thoughts about things that mystify him, relationships and the "Thong Song."

items.title: Oh, Hello on Broadway
items.overview: Two delusional geriatrics reveal curious pasts, share a love of tuna and welcome a surprise guest in this filming of the popular Broadway comedy show.

items.listTitle: Sarah Silverman: A Speck of Dust
items.title: Sarah Silverman: A Speck of Dust
items.overview: In her first comedy special post-health scare, Sarah Silverman shares a mix of fun facts, sad truths and yeah-she-just-went-there moments.

items.title: Kanan Gill: Keep It Real
items.overview: In this hilarious one hour comedy special, Kanan Gill squints at a variety of subjects ranging from the difficulty in talking to your parents to The Constitution of India. It's easy to keep it funny. Kanan keeps it real.

items.title: Hasan Minhaj: Homecoming King
items.overview: Comic Hasan Minhaj of "The Daily Show" shares personal stories about racism, immigrant parents, prom night horrors and more in this stand-up special.

items.title: Tracy Morgan: Staying Alive
items.overview: In his first special since his serious car accident, Tracy Morgan cracks jokes about life in a coma, his second marriage and his family's dark side.

items.listTitle: Norm Macdonald: Hitler's Dog, Gossip & Trickery
items.title: Norm Macdonald: Hitler's Dog, Gossip & Trickery
items.overview: Norm Macdonald delivers sly, deadpan observations from an older — and perhaps even wiser — point of view in this special.

items.title: Chris Gethard: Career Suicide
items.overview: A comedy about depression, alcoholism, suicide and the other funniest parts of life. Gethard holds nothing back as he dives into his experiences with mental illness and psychiatry, finding hope in the strangest places. An adaption of his one-man off-Broadway show of the same name.

items.title: Maria Bamford: Old Baby
items.overview: She's savagely upbeat. Lovably awkward. And full of surprises. A wildly funny trip through a one-of-a-kind comic mind.

items.title: Vir Das: Abroad Understanding
items.overview: Comedian Vir Das tackles nationalism, globalism, good food and bad politics in two cleverly crosscut performances in New York and New Delhi.

items.listTitle: Kenny Sebastian: Don't Be That Guy
items.title: Kenny Sebastian: Don't Be That Guy
items.overview: In his 5th stand-up special, Paavam (Innocent) comedian Kenny Sebastian talks about moving cities, his parents and why he is a former nice guy.

items.title: Lucas Brothers: On Drugs
items.overview: Deadpan twin comics Keith and Kenny Lucas take the stage in Brooklyn with a set that touches on drugs, race, Deion Sanders, teachers and O.J. Simpson.

items.title: Louis C.K. 2017
items.overview: Louis C.K. muses on religion, eternal love, giving dogs drugs, email fights, teachers and more in a live performance from Washington, D.C.

items.title: Jo Koy: Live from Seattle
items.overview: Between raising a teenage boy and growing up with a Filipino mother, stand-up comic Jo Koy has been through a lot. He's here to tell you all about it.

items.listTitle: Dave Chappelle: The Age of Spin
items.title: Dave Chappelle: The Age of Spin
items.overview: Comedy icon Dave Chappelle makes his triumphant return to the screen with a pair of blistering, fresh stand-up specials. Filmed at The Palladium in Los Angeles, California, in March 2016.

items.listTitle: Dave Chappelle: Deep in the Heart of Texas
items.title: Dave Chappelle: Deep in the Heart of Texas
items.overview: Comedy icon Dave Chappelle makes his triumphant return to the screen with a pair of blistering, fresh stand-up specials. Filmed at the Moody Theater in Austin, Texas, in April 2015.

items.title: Jim Norton: Mouthful of Shame
items.overview: Fedoras, mom's underpants, and puppy love all make Jim Norton's s**t list in 'Mouthful of Shame'.

items.title: Jerrod Carmichael: 8
items.overview: Performing in the round and engaging audience members during his act, Carmichael addresses a wide range of subjects, including Trump’s victory, climate change, supporting the troops, animal rights, being a good boyfriend and his top four fears, as well as exploring larger themes like race, politics, love and family.

items.title: Amy Schumer: The Leather Special
items.overview: Comic sensation Amy Schumer riffs on sex, dating and the absurdities of fame in a bold and uncensored stand-up set at Denver's Bellco Theater.

items.title: Kurt Braunohler: Trust Me
items.overview: Kurt Braunohler shines a light on the hidden absurdities of life, lending his self-effacing point of view to everything from the controversial to the mundane. He dives into the dregs of reality TV, gives damning praise to dogs for their boundless loyalty, and shares a plan to undermine white male privilege that might just be crazy enough to work.

items.listTitle: Mike Birbiglia: Thank God for Jokes
items.title: Mike Birbiglia: Thank God for Jokes
